A better way to put it would probably be: Nobody can truly protect your privacy in a meaningful way except for: you.

I fear that there is going to be no way around the fact that for privacy: you are going to have work for it. You're going to have to understand encryption tools. You're going to have to understand how to use TOR. You're going to have to learn how JavaScript can make you vulnerable even when using these tools, and all the little "Gotcha's!" that can foil even a moderately tech savvy person.

Even when a company wants to try and make this all easier and more transparent for your average user, they can only go so far before they start compromising security. You basically trade security for convenience, or convenience for security. I don't think there will ever truly be a way around this. The better the privacy you want, the more work and first hand knowledge you will have to have.

The only reason you aren't paying for Facebook, or Gmail, or Pintrest, or Google Photos, etc etc etc is because you are paying for it with your privacy. It all sure is pretty damn convenient though aint it?

You can have all the privacy you want, but nobody can be expected to do it for you. Even if Google starts encrypting everything tomorrow, and providing as much privacy and security as they possibly can: They are still a 3rd party point of failure.
